doc.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995

title: First European tours with Lena Horne and Helen Humes
summary: He first went overseas in 1950 with Horne, playing the London Palladium, and later toured yearly with Humes for George Wein.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Any chances to go overseas with some of the singers?

Oh yeah. My first time overseas was with Lena Horne. That was 1950. That was a ball because I got a chance to play the London Palladium, you know, and that was, to me, really something. And we traveled all over Europe. We went to Spain, Sweden, [inaudible] wherever that is, Belgium I guess. It was a ball. And then when I joined Helen Humes we used to go over every year with George Wein’s jazz thing. So I spent a lot of time in Europe. I made a lot of friends over there.
